sections.skill: Distinguish contributing from investing in an IRA and track contributions, earnings, and returns

questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: Taylor contributed $500 to a Roth IRA, but the money remains in the account's cash position. What has Taylor not necessarily done yet?
questions.intro: Contributing moves money into the IRA. The money often lands in a cash or money market position. Investing is a separate step: choosing and buying funds or other investments.
questions.feedback: Money in the cash position has been contributed but not yet invested.
questions.topic: Contributing to and investing inside an IRA
sources: Hypothetical example; no changing rule is used.

questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: Taylor wants one broadly diversified investment for a retirement 45 years away. Which choice fits?

choices.text: All of it in a single small company's stock
A savings account inside the IRA, forever
A short-term CD that is renewed every month for decades
A low-cost target-date fund near the year she turns 65

questions.correct_answer: A low-cost target-date fund near the year she turns 65
questions.intro: Common IRA investments include index funds and target-date funds. A target-date fund holds a diversified mix of stock and bond funds and becomes more conservative as its target year approaches.
questions.feedback: A target-date fund offers broad diversification in one choice.
questions.topic: Contributing to and investing inside an IRA
sources: Hypothetical example; no changing rule is used.

questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: Over several years, Ana contributed $6,000 to her Roth IRA. It is now worth $7,800. How much are earnings?
questions.intro: In an IRA, contributions are the money you put in; earnings are the growth (dividends, interest, and gains). Balance = contributions + earnings.
questions.topic: Contributing to and investing inside an IRA
sources: Hypothetical example; no changing rule is used.

questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: Ana's $7,800 Roth IRA falls 10% in a market drop. What is it worth, and what are her total contributions?
questions.intro: Investments in an IRA can rise or fall. A loss lowers the balance but does not change how much you contributed.
questions.topic: Contributing to and investing inside an IRA
sources: Hypothetical example; no changing rule is used.

questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: Why does compounding work especially well in a Roth IRA?

choices.text: Earnings grow without yearly taxes and qualified withdrawals are tax-free
Roth IRAs cannot go down in value
The provider pays a guaranteed bonus rate

questions.correct_answer: Earnings grow without yearly taxes and qualified withdrawals are tax-free
questions.feedback: No yearly tax drag, and tax-free qualified withdrawals, let more of the growth compound.
questions.topic: Contributing to and investing inside an IRA

misconceptions.D: Confuses an IRA with a bank promotion

sections.relationship: The cash-versus-invested confusion is the most common IRA mistake; this branch isolates it.

questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: Money that is contributed to an IRA but not invested usually earns…

choices.text: only the low rate of the cash or money market position
nothing ever, and it is lost after a year

questions.correct_answer: only the low rate of the cash or money market position
questions.intro: Uninvested cash in an IRA typically sits in a money market fund or bank sweep that pays a modest rate.
questions.feedback: Cash earns only the cash rate until invested.
questions.topic: Contributing to and investing inside an IRA
sources: Hypothetical example; no changing rule is used.

questions.prompt: Taylor's target-date fund has a 0.12% expense ratio. On a $10,000 balance, what is the yearly cost?

questions.prompt: Which number determines how much Taylor can withdraw from her Roth IRA anytime without tax or penalty?
questions.intro: Roth IRA contributions can be withdrawn at any time without tax or penalty; earnings follow stricter rules.
questions.feedback: Contributions (not earnings) can come out anytime tax- and penalty-free.

questions.intro: Market drops are normal over long periods. Panic selling can lock in losses.
questions.feedback: Selling in a panic turns a temporary drop into a permanent loss.

questions.prompt: Taylor sells one fund and buys another inside her Roth IRA. Does she owe tax on the sale this year?

choices.text: No; trades inside an IRA are not taxed when made
Only if she made a profit

questions.correct_answer: No; trades inside an IRA are not taxed when made
questions.intro: Buying and selling within an IRA does not create current taxes.
questions.feedback: IRA trades are sheltered; only withdrawals follow tax rules.
